instruction: Use web-first assertions; never verify element state with one-shot reads
relevant_when: Test code asserts on element state, text, visibility or counts
context: expect(locator) matchers retry until they pass or time out. Reads such as textContent(), innerText(), inputValue(), isVisible() and count() evaluate once, so asserting on their result races with rendering. Every test must also assert the behavior its title promises.

checklist.name: web-first-assertions
checklist.rule: Element state, text and counts are asserted with expect(locator).toBeVisible/toHaveText/toContainText/toHaveCount/toBeEnabled, not by reading a value and asserting on it
checklist.relevant_when: A test or page-object method checks element content or state

checklist.name: no-swallowed-state-checks
checklist.rule: isVisible().catch(() => false) probes are limited to genuinely optional UI, are not issued immediately after an action without a wait, and never replace an assertion; prefer locator.or() or a short waitFor
checklist.relevant_when: A test branches on whether an element is present

checklist.name: assertion-present
checklist.rule: Confirm the test explicitly verifies its intended outcome, including through a helper or another check the scanner may not recognize
checklist.relevant_when: A test is added or changed

checklist.name: assertion-matches-title
checklist.rule: The asserted outcome actually matches what the test title claims; a test titled for a cart update asserts the cart, not just that a page loaded
checklist.relevant_when: A test is added or changed

checklist.name: no-vacuous-negatives
checklist.rule: A not.toBeVisible()/toHaveCount(0) assertion is preceded by a positive precondition so it cannot pass because the page never loaded
checklist.relevant_when: A test asserts something is absent
